invariants: Decision.approval_status == 'approved' and Decision.approved_by matches ^human(:<name>)?$ for every record (only a human approval creates a record; records never self-authorize, ADR-060)
Decision.staged_at == Decision.approved_at (staging is automatic: the run stages the record the moment the human approves)
Decision.staged_path == '<run_root>/runs/' + run_id + '/staged/decisions/' + id + '.yaml' for every record (every record is staged in its run before it can be published)
Decision.lifecycle_stage == 'staged' iff Decision.record_path == null iff Decision.review_state == 'not-published'
Decision.record_path == 'docs/decisions/' + id + '.yaml' iff Decision.lifecycle_stage in {published, superseded}

Decision.lifecycle_stage == 'superseded' iff Decision.superseded_by != [] iff Decision.corrections != [] (only `decisions publish --correct` supersedes a record, appending one correction per superseding record and changing nothing else)
Decision.superseded_by contains B iff record B.supersedes contains this Decision.id, and each correction's superseded_by names one of them
Decision.selected_option_id resolves to one of its options[].id, and Decision.selected_option_title equals that option's title
Decision.title == Decision.selected_option_title, shortened by the kernel with ' ...' when long

Decision.assessment_basis == 'precedent_reuse' iff exactly one precedents_considered entry has action 'reused'; such a record has criteria == [], selected_rank == null, confidence == null, and its single option is proposed_by 'precedent:<that id>'

Decision.assessment_basis == 'kernel_ranking' implies the options' kernel_rank values are 1..n without gaps, required_mean does not increase with rank, selected_rank == the selected option's kernel_rank, and confidence == that option's required_mean

Decision.precedents_considered[].action follows applicability: below 0.5 -> not_applicable; 0.5 or above -> used_as_evidence; 0.8 or above is offered for reuse only when the decision had no options of its own and the precedent is not superseded, and the human's answer turns the note into reused or set_aside
Decision.related == the precedents_considered ids whose action != 'not_applicable'
Decision.supersedes contains P iff its precedents_considered note for P has action 'set_aside' and the human chose a different option than P did
No Decision cites a superseded precedent with action 'reused' (a superseded record is never offered for reuse)
Decision.considered_by lists exactly the records whose precedents_considered names this id, with that record's action (a derived reverse view for display, not a field of the record file)
Decision.publish_command == 'python -m kernel decisions publish --run-id ' + run_id, followed by ' --correct <id> --reason "..."' for each id in Decision.supersedes

fields.id: string — kernel-minted record id, dec-<16 hex>; the file name in docs/decisions/
fields.title: string — the record's title as filed: the selected option's title (the kernel shortens a long one with ' ...')
fields.question: string — the question the run decided (trimmed from the record's `question`)
fields.lifecycle_stage: enum: staged | published | superseded — staged == only in the run root, awaiting `decisions publish`; published == written into docs/decisions/ with the index regenerated; superseded == published, then corrected by a later record via `publish --correct`. Being reused as precedent is not a stage: see considered_by
fields.review_state: enum: not-published | in-review | merged — where the published record stands in normal git review (not-published while staged)
fields.publish_pr: string | null — the pull request carrying the published record through review (e.g. '#979'); null while staged, and on illustrative records
fields.assessment_basis: enum: kernel_ranking | precedent_reuse — kernel_ranking == formed by research, Jev's per-criterion assessment and a human ranked choice; precedent_reuse == formed by the human confirming a precedent offered for reuse
fields.criteria: array of { id, priority: required | supporting, question } — the criteria the human approved while forming (empty for a reuse)
fields.options: array of { id, title, proposed_by: caller_goal | host.generate_options | human:<name> | precedent:<dec id>, kernel_rank: integer | null, required_mean: number | null, required_passed: integer | null, required_total: integer | null } — listed in kernel rank order; rank fields are null for a reuse
fields.selected_rank: integer | null — the kernel's rank of the chosen option (null for a reuse); a human may choose below rank 1
fields.confidence: number | null — the chosen option's required-criteria mean (null for a reuse)
fields.approval_status: enum: approved — every record is human-approved
fields.approved_at: string — ISO-8601 UTC time of the human approval
fields.staged_at: string — ISO-8601 UTC time the run staged the record (provenance.created_at)
fields.precedents_considered: array of { id: dec id, applicability: number 0..1, action: used_as_evidence | offered_for_reuse | reused | set_aside | not_applicable, note } — earlier records the run's precedent search judged for this decision
fields.considered_by: array of { id: dec id, action } — later records whose precedents_considered names this one (derived reverse view: how this record was retrieved as precedent)
fields.related: array of dec ids — precedents judged applicable
fields.supersedes: array of dec ids — earlier records this decision replaces (the human decided anew and chose differently)
fields.superseded_by: array of dec ids — later records that replaced this one
fields.corrections: array of { corrected_at, corrected_by: human:<name>, reason, superseded_by: dec id, new_selected_option_id } — append-only, written by `publish --correct`
fields.components: array of component ids from docs/components.json (retrieval filter)
fields.roadmap_phase: array of roadmap phase ids (retrieval filter)
fields.repository_wide: boolean — retrieval filter: applies across the whole repository
fields.run_id: string — the kernel run that formed and staged the record (run-<16 hex>)
fields.langfuse_trace_id: string — the run's Langfuse trace id
fields.staged_path: string — where the run staged the record; <run_root> is the machine-local kernel run root
fields.record_path: string | null — docs/decisions/<id>.yaml once published; null while staged
fields.publish_command: string — the command a human runs to publish this record from its run (with --correct for each record it supersedes)
fields.source: string — where this sample record comes from: a real published or staged record, or an illustrative one for a state the real store has not reached

provenance.note: The ONE canonical Decision dataset for decision_kernel (decision-lifecycle product truth). Four records mirror the real decision store: the first record (published, merged in PR #978, reused and cited as precedent), the two records published for review in PR #979, and one record staged by a precedent reuse and never published. Long text is trimmed; evidence lists, per-criterion scores and repository revisions are left out. Two records marked illustrative cover the superseded state, which no real record has reached yet. Extend this dataset; do not start a second Decision dataset.
